findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees practice adequate handwashing before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training certification during today’s inspection. PIC said that those documents were locked away and they had no access to them. Inspector told PIC to have copies of certifications in a folder accessible for inspection purposes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.comment:
Observed the steam table was not hot holding foods at 135F or above. The water in the steam table had an ambient air temperature of 136F which an employee stated was much lower than usual. The gravy had an internal temperature of 120F and a brown sauce had an internal temperature of 107F. Other foods in the steam table included a casserole and various other sauces. The PIC stated the foods were set in the steam table this morning and they go through them very quickly. All the sauces were reheated back up to 165F. The inspector created a paper with the name of the food, the time it was set in the steam table, and the time it must be discarded. When the time the food must be discarded is reached, the food cannot be saved; it must be thrown away. The facility should use time as control for the foods in the steam table until it can hot hold foods at the proper temperature. When new foods are put in the steam table the discard time must be written on the paper. The inspector suggests getting immediate service on the steam table. The inspector will return on 09/10/2024 to check on the steam table temperature. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
(SECOND REPEAT) A gap along the bottom of the back door allowing daylight through was observed during inspection.  Outside doors not completely sealed from the outside elements can allow for pest, rodent, and weather entry.  Ensure the seal around the door is repaired/replaced.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
(SECOND REPEAT) The hood was observed to contain an accumulation of grease and dust debris.  The hood and hood baffles are in need of being cleaned in between professional cleaning services.  Ensure this is done to prevent contamination of food from grease dripping on the grill into the food. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed a small leak coming from the central portion of the tripe sink faucet. Ensure that plumbing systems are maintained in good repair. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(SECOND REPEAT) There are two holes in the wall on the left side of the back hallway.  The holes in the wall may allow for pest and rodent entry/harborage.  These areas are also not able to be properly cleaned of soil and food debris.  Ensure the holes are fixed to create a smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent surface.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(SECOND REPEAT) Areas that need to be recaulked or sealed:
-Mop basin
-Along the 3 part sink
Ensure these areas are sealed/caulked to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface.


6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness training had recently expired. The PIC stated they will be getting the training renewed soon. Ensure that CFPM’s obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
